workload: Unmodified HBase 2.6.6 JUnit 5 test and its HBaseTestingUtility.startMiniCluster(1), with embedded ZooKeeper and HDFS; no Docker or handwritten workload.
source_review: The unmodified JUnit creates enabled tables and reaches HBaseAdmin.flushAsync through four admin.flush calls. The selected guard calls isTableEnabled, which reads TableState via MetaTableAccessor.getTableState and compares it with ENABLED. The tested transient meta-read/RPC exceptions were retried by HBaseAdmin.executeCallable/RpcRetryingCallerImpl; post-write acknowledgement faults did not make the selected table disabled. Every JUnit run passed, no selected exception occurred after an effective fault, and no new bug was confirmed in this workload.
provenance_gate_note: Phase 1/2 trials use GraphChecker woven classes and static region skeleton for occurrence identity. Retain as historical evidence; independent graph-free method completion requires ByteBuddy/JaCoCo healthy and representative replay, then a decision on a new campaign.

legacy_graph_next_action: Run case-local ByteBuddy/JaCoCo original JUnit healthy and representative fault selectors, then start a fresh graph-free campaign if identity and target are retained
legacy_graph_limitations: Conclusion applies to this original one-region-server embedded-cluster JUnit workload and these observed I/O doors; other workloads and failure models remain untested.
The state-write trial matched by full occurrence/site/ordinal but its server thread had no registered sourceKey; the four read trials and the two-fault mutation had a registered client sourceKey.
legacy_graph_methodology_note: Graph-free fault selection and feedback only: source-nearby runtime I/O identities, exact marker/site/occurrence/sourceKey/ordinal replay, and method/branch coverage drive mutation; no aggregate causal graph or closure is constructed or consulted. Tracing and identity still use GraphChecker weaving and static region skeletons.
legacy_graph_budget_label_note: Two early 5/6-fault trials retain their historical exploratory_outside_default_budget label from the former 48/4 policy; they count toward the current 64/6 budget because exact faults were applied and the target remained reachable.

quality_completion_note: Original TestMobStoreScanner.testMobStoreScanner completed 84 exact I/O fault-sequence attempts (max 8 ordered faults); 80 retained the selected flushAsync check after the final fault. Four post-target final faults were excluded from the effective budget. All 84 original JUnit runs passed and none threw the selected TableNotEnabledException. JaCoCo production probes increased by 40. The last 16 effective trials yielded no new production probes or stable I/O families, so the 128-trial extension criterion was false.
